title: Google Chat API: Auth Types and Quotas (2026 Guide)
summary: The googlechat api is a REST service for managing spaces and messages. You can set it up, understand rate limits, and resolve common errors.
body_markdown:
## Connect Google Chat to other tools with Activepieces


Activepieces, an open-source automation platform, has a Google Chat integration. It lets a workflow post into a space when something happens in another tool, so the "post the result later" step needs no API code of your own.


It doesn't remove the auth decision or the quota problem.


### When a no-code workflow is enough


Use it when the message is a notification: a deploy finished, a form was submitted, a ticket changed state. The workflow starts from a trigger in some other tool, formats a message, and posts it with a Google Chat action.


Activepieces holds the connection, so you're not storing credentials in a script someone will forget about.


Worth using early: the builder's test mode. The screenshot below shows a single step, "1. Chat UI", a Human Input action, with a Published Chat URL for production viewing and a Draft Chat URL for testing and generating sample data.


Treat the draft URL as your sandbox: run the flow there until the data shape is right, and only then publish.


Note that this step is Activepieces' own chat front end, not Google Chat, so it's a way to exercise a flow, not a substitute for testing the post into a real space.


### When you still need the API directly


Stop reaching for the canvas when you need control over how a request fails. An integration gives you a step that either worked or errored.


It doesn't give you your own backoff policy, request-level handling of quota responses, or deduplication so a retried run doesn't post the same message twice. Those are the retry-first design problems this article keeps returning to.


Go to the API directly when:


- the message must come from a specific identity and you need to choose the auth mode yourself
- you need to update or delete a message you posted earlier, tracked by its ID
- volume is high enough that quotas shape the design


If a Google Chat action you need isn't in the catalogue, you don't wait on a vendor's roadmap: you can build the missing integration yourself, with AI assisting, and keep it private to your own Activepieces instance.


It helps that roughly 60% of the 750 integrations, counted from the open-source monorepo, were built by the community.
